mainEntity.name: What Should Be Included in an Agency Delivery SOP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Five stages with a gate condition between each, a named owner per stage, and three templates: scope sheet, build checklist, launch checklist. Anything more is documentation you'll stop maintaining by March.

mainEntity.name: How Long Does It Take to Document a Delivery SOP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Four weeks at two hours a week, provided you write it alongside live projects. Working from a project in front of you beats working from memory, because memory edits out every bit where you improvised.

mainEntity.name: Should a Freelancer Use One, or Is It Only for Teams?

acceptedAnswer.text: Freelancers benefit more. No colleague catches what you missed, so the checklist is your second pair of eyes, and the scope sheet lets you refuse a request by pointing at a document rather than at yourself.

mainEntity.name: How Many Clients Can a Three-Person Agency Handle?

acceptedAnswer.text: Six to eight concurrent builds, with two or three active and the rest parked at a gate. A project waiting at a gate costs you nothing. A project in an undefined state costs you a check-in every day.

mainEntity.name: Does an SOP Make the Work Feel Generic?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only if you standardise the wrong half. Sequence, checks and admin should be identical every time. Design and strategy shouldn't be touched at all.

HowTo.name: How to build an agency delivery SOP
HowTo.description: A five-stage delivery SOP with a gate between each stage, designed so a three-person agency can run at the throughput of a much larger team.

step.name: Lock the scope
step.text: Produce a one-page scope sheet covering page count, who supplies copy and images, integrations in and out, number of review rounds, and what happens to the launch date when content arrives late. Gate: signed scope sheet.

step.name: Run the build kickoff
step.text: Select from four or five standardised templates, create the project, and collect client content into one place. Set a fixed build window, ten working days is a realistic default. Gate: all client-supplied content received.

step.name: Run internal QA before the client sees anything
step.text: Someone who did not build the site works the QA checklist cold: forms, internal links, metadata, image compression and alt text, mobile rendering, analytics, SSL and the 404 page. Gate: checklist signed off by a second person.

step.name: Run one bounded review round
step.text: Give the client one comprehensive round through a single feedback channel with a five working day deadline, then a corrections-only second round. Quote anything outside the signed scope. Gate: written sign-off.

step.name: Launch and hand over
step.text: Connect the domain, verify SSL, map redirects, submit the sitemap, confirm analytics and schedule backups. Send a one-page handover pack. Gate: handover delivered and the project closed.
